text.p: Portuguese bonds were down slightly in thin trade and dealers expected a quiet session with U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving.
"Italy and Spain are lower but our futures and 10-year bonds have not fallen to the same extent. Spreads under Spanish Bonos have widened," said one dealer.
"The shorter and medium-term maturities still look strongest while 10-year bonds will continue to look to neighbouring markets for direction," another trader said.
Dealers expected the spread under 10-year Bonos to remain at between 10 and 15 basis points.

"There shouldn't be much of a downward correction in longer maturities because the yield spread over German Bunds is 124 basis points and that's where it's been consolidating recently," one dealer said.
"Of course if Spain takes a tumble we'll fall too, but not as far," he added.
The Bank of Portugal injected 30 billion escudos into the money market at an average weighted 6.90 percent.
Overnight/tomorrow next rates rose accordingly to 6.86/6.89 percent from 6.75/6.80 percent. The escudo stood at 101.00/03 per mark after opening at 100.98/101.00.
